audit_findings.title: The DCF, bridge, and share denominator may represent different economic claims because of Timken India’s large noncontrolling interest
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable earnings, consolidated owner-earnings adjustments, consolidated cash and debt, and parent diluted shares may use inconsistent ownership perimeters.
audit_findings.evidence: The sale reduced the Company’s ownership in TIL from 57.70 percent to 51.05 percent.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a substantial noncontrolling claim: Timken owns only 51.05% of TIL, latest noncontrolling interest is $168.6 million, and 2025 net income attributable to noncontrolling interests was $28.9 million, equal to 8.2% of the $351.2 million OE anchor. The supplied record does not establish the precise OE construction or subsidiary-level cash, debt, depreciation, and capital expenditure allocation, so the valuation error is not yet quantified. Because the mismatch can affect both recurring OE and the equity bridge, it is reasonably capable of materially changing intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE and the bridge on a consistent parent-attributable basis, or value consolidated operations and deduct the fair economic value of noncontrolling interests; reconcile TIL earnings, depreciation, capex, cash, and debt explicitly.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded retirement obligations are claims ahead of common equity but are absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $190.7 million gross 2025 pension and postretirement deficit; $35 million expected 2026 contributions and payments
audit_findings.mechanism: Any deficit not already absorbed through normalized cash OE is a debt-like bridge deduction; contributions exceeding normalized expense also reduce recurring OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The projected benefit obligation and the accumulated benefit obligations at December 31, 2025 exceeded the market value of plan assets for most of the Company's pension plans.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation is demonstrated: the 2025 pension deficit was $157.7 million and the unfunded postretirement obligation was $33.0 million, totaling $190.7 million before tax effects. That equals 5.8% of the $3,273 million base equity value, or $2.70 per diluted share. Expected 2026 pension and postretirement cash requirements total $35 million, approximately 10.0% of anchor OE. The record does not show how much is already captured in normalized OE, so the incremental correction remains unresolved but is potentially material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile pension and postretirement expense, cash contributions, and OE adjustments; obtain the latest funded deficits and tax effects, then rerun OE and deduct only the residual debt-like claim to avoid double counting.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may require acquisition spending that the owner-earnings forecast does not fund
audit_findings.magnitude: $124.4 million 2026 acquisition outlay; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition consideration required to achieve forecast growth would reduce future owner earnings or require an explicit reinvestment deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Net sales increased in 2025 compared to 2024 primarily due to the favorable impact of acquisitions of $38 million as well as the favorable impact of foreign currency exchange of $17 million, partially offset by lower organic sales of $46 million (lower demand, favorable pricing).
audit_findings.explanation: The concern is plausible but not demonstrated as a valuation error. Acquisitions contributed $38 million of 2025 sales while organic sales declined $46 million, and the company spent $124.4 million on an acquisition in the first half of 2026. Conversely, first-half 2026 organic revenue increased $101 million, so the record does not establish that the 3% base or 6% bull growth rates require recurring acquisitions. The OE contribution and recurring purchase price needed to sustain either growth case are unavailable.
audit_findings.action: Develop an organic OE growth series excluding acquired operations, quantify OE obtained per dollar of acquisition spending, and rerun the base and bull cases with either supported organic growth or explicit recurring acquisition reinvestment.

audit_findings.title: Not all cash added in the bridge may be freely distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: $372.5 million of foreign cash; required haircut unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Restricted, operationally required, tax-burdened, or noncontrolling-owned cash should be excluded or discounted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Repatriation of non-U.S. cash could be subject to taxes and some portion may be subject to governmental restrictions.
audit_findings.explanation: At June 30, 2026, $372.5 million, or 93.3%, of the filed $399.1 million cash balance was outside the United States. It represents 11.4% of the $3,273 million base equity value and $5.27 per diluted share before considering short-term investments. The filing confirms possible taxes and restrictions, while TIL’s minority ownership creates an additional allocation issue. The record does not quantify the trapped amount, tax leakage, operational minimum, or minority share, but the exposed balance is large enough to be material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain cash and short-term investments by jurisdiction and legal entity, identify restricted and minimum operating cash, allocate TIL balances by economic ownership, calculate repatriation leakage, and rerun the bridge with distributable cash only.

audit_findings.title: A nonrecurring tax release may inflate the FY2025 owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $13.2 million anchor adjustment; computed base-value effect approximately $185.4 million or $2.62 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: An unnormalized discrete tax benefit increases the OE anchor and is then compounded and capitalized throughout the DCF.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, the Company recorded $13.2 million of net tax benefit for uncertain tax positions, which consisted primarily of $21.0 million of the net reversal of accruals for prior year uncertain tax positions and settlements with tax authorities.
audit_findings.explanation: The $13.2 million net uncertain-tax-position benefit is filed and equals 3.8% of the $351.2 million OE anchor. If fully embedded and unnormalized, proportional application of the base operating-PV-to-anchor multiple produces an approximately $185.4 million reduction in base equity value, or $2.62 per share, equal to 5.7% of base equity value. The record does not establish whether the OE schedule already reversed the benefit, so this is a potentially material unresolved error rather than a demonstrated double count.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $13.2 million benefit through parent-attributable net income and the FY2025 OE schedule; if not already removed, normalize it and rerun every scenario and the buy-below threshold.

audit_findings.title: Government-incentive clawbacks create additional debt-like cash claims omitted from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $20.1 million Spinea exposure; $39.1 million total recorded 2025 government assistance liabilities
audit_findings.mechanism: Probable repayments not already reflected in OE would be deducted as debt-like claims in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: While the Company is hopeful that Spinea will meet it obligation to create the 450 new jobs, the Company has recorded a potential shortfall of $ 20.1 million, including interest, in other non-current liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The $20.1 million Spinea potential shortfall is recorded, but it equals only 0.6% of the $3,273 million base equity value, or $0.28 per diluted share. Even treating all $39.1 million of recorded 2025 government-assistance liabilities as immediately repayable would reduce base value by only 1.2%, or $0.55 per share. That scale would not materially change the valuation range or conclusion, although any later increase should be monitored through filings.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the latest Spinea compliance position and government-assistance liability breakdown; deduct probable repayments in the next rerun, but no separate material valuation escalation is warranted at the filed scale.
